content.text:
I've submitted index 13 (Pb 0.34 / Sb 0.66) as the best composition, but every measured EQE was essentially zero, so it's a weak result. I used all 3 merit measurements and all 5 XRD measurements.

**How I chose what to measure:** I spent the XRD budget first, on indices 4, 9, 13, 19 and 26 spread along the composition line, to see which crystal phases were present.
- The Pb-rich end (index 4) is dominated by a phase with a strong peak at Q≈2.045 Å⁻¹.
- The middle, indices 9 and 13, shows lead antimonate (PbSb₂O₆) reflections, strongest at index 13, which is close to that compound's 1:2 Pb:Sb ratio.
- The Sb-rich end (index 26) looks like antimony oxide. I expected it to absorb little light at 3.2 eV, so I didn't spend a merit measurement there.

**EQE results:**

| Index | Pb / Sb | Phase (from XRD) | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.34 / 0.66 | Nearly pure PbSb₂O₆ | **+0.00045** |
| 9 | 0.48 / 0.52 | PbSb₂O₆ plus the Pb-rich phase | −0.00083 |
| 3 | 0.69 / 0.31 | Pb-rich phase (inferred from its neighbour, index 4) | −0.0021 |

Index 13 was the only positive value. The three results differ by only thousandths of a percent and are probably within measurement noise. This library appears to be a very weak photoanode system under 3.2 eV light. It's also possible the best composition is somewhere I didn't measure, especially the Sb-rich end or the region around index 19.
